title: Buying a three-dollar trombone and joining the Tuskegee second band
summary: Hearing the Tuskegee band makes him want a horn; Owens finds him a trombone and Captain Frank Dryer has it repaired and puts him in the second band.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the horn: first instrument and the trombone

blocks.x: The thing was these were what we called natives. They had money and got into something and were very careless around. Anyway, I entered school and went onto school and everything was going on there and then nicely and then when I'd get to hear the orchestra, to go into the dining room, and that band, the Tuskegee
Band, I said I've got to play some kind of horn. It went to the band director, Captain Dryer--
Now, at Tuskegee?
Yes.
They had a band too at the restaurant?
Yes, in our dining room, the orchestra played, then they had the marching band, the big band. They had a big band.

So Captain Dryer was the band director and so I went to see Captain Dryer and I told him I'd like to get in the second band. I said I know a little about music and he said that's fine, what horn, what do you want to play and I said I want to play anything, I just want to play. He started laughing and he said that's all right, but what horn do you have? I said (inaudible).
Anyway, he was very nice and he said I hope you can figure out something. He

went on, and he said, my goodness, I remember your brother here. Why in the world didn't Clarence make you get a horn before you came here or something. So we went on and one of my classmates, Owens--
Wait a minute. What was the band director's name again?
Frank L. Dryer.
Dryer?
YES. D-R-Y-E-R.
That's Tuskegee?
That's Tuskegee.

So, I got to talking with Owens, my classmate, who was a trumpet player, and I said, I sure wish I could be in that band. He called and asked a few questions about music and he said you know a little bit and I said, I had one or two lessons on the piano, but I was too lazy to practice and this and that, but I want a horn. So he finally said what kind of

horn and I told him just like I said to Captain Dryer. I said any instrument, but I want to get in that band. He said I'll look around. So one day he came to me and said, Ernie, Ernie, I said what, there's this band--there's this trombone that he wants to sell and I said I don't have--and he said he'll sell it cheap, he just wants some money, he's broke and he wants some money. So he took me to this guy and this guy said yeah, I'll sell you the trombone. I said what do you want for it; he said six dollars. I said I don't have six dollars; you don't even have six dollars, I'm almost giving it to you. I said no, I don't have no six dollars; what do you have? And so I said I have three dollars, and he said (inaudible), but I'm going to let you have it for the three, but now you owe me three dollars. So I told him okay, and so I took the trombone.
So I went to Captain Dryer, he said well, you have a horn, but you can't use this. I'll tell you what, Fields,seeing that

you're determined and I am going to send this out to be repaired, and I thanked him, and so he sent the horn away and when it came back it was in pretty nice shape and all and then I went to go in the second band, starting from the beginning and taking lessons in the second. band.
That was the latter part of the year. About the middle of the year when I got the horn--it was the latter part of the school term.
